subject: URGENT: Skyline Retail throughput collapse - peer gateway + DNS instability
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 16:08:00 +0000
Subject: Skyline Retail - sudden latency & 5xx spike (alert)

Team,

Alert from Skyline's token queues this morning: 3x median latency and a 12% 5xx rate across the us-west cluster starting ~15:30 UTC. They've reported timeouts from their checkout flow and we have a backlog building on several routes.

Initial symptoms from our side:
- Elevated request queueing on pool-us-west-1 (increased GQL queue depth).
- Rapid conntrack table growth on the gateway nodes (see attached conntrack_dump_region-us-11-30.txt).
- DNS failures observed in the app logs: repeated NXDOMAIN / SERVFAIL to our resolver cluster.

Customer impact: Skyline noted degraded UX for ~45 minutes; they've escalated to their ops@ address and are asking for an exec call.

Can infra/network take a look ASAP? I pushed the raw conntrack sample and a short PCAP to the incident drive link.

Attachments: conntrack_dump_region-us-11-30.txt, dns_trace_skyline_1130.pcap

—Ben
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, ops@skyline-retail.com
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 16:22:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Skyline Retail - sudden latency & 5xx spike (alert)

Acknowledged — triage in progress.

Quick notes from initial triage (infra):
- We see rapid NAT session churn on the egress gateway cluster in us-west-1 causing ephemeral port exhaustion on a subset of gateways. That correlates with the conntrack dump Ben attached.
- Concurrently, the resolver pool in us-west experienced intermittent SERVFAILs for ~7 minutes (11:33–11:40 UTC); likely upstream resolver health flapping.
- Traffic shaping rules for Skyline's VPC peering route were re-applied by an automated policy at 11:31 UTC (we're pulling audit logs now).

Immediate actions we are executing:
1) Remove the affected gateway nodes from the pool and force failover to healthy egress nodes (ETA 10 min).
2) Bypass automated route policy re-application for Skyline's peering for the next 6 hours while we stabilize.
3) Roll forward an emergency conntrack threshold increase on the gateway nodes to prevent immediate session exhaustion.

Asking Jordan to pull a packet capture and correlate with our NAT counters and resolver logs. Ben, please let the Skyline ops team know we have mitigation in flight and request any client-side logs they can share for the exact time window.

—Marissa
Director, Customer Reliability

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 16:33:47 +0000
Subject: Skyline packet capture + resolver timeline
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Attached: dns_trace_skyline_1130.pcap — highlights below.

Highlights from the PCAP and metrics:
- Repeated outbound SYNs from multiple client IPs that never complete the handshake to our gateway (RSTs returned) — suggests middlebox interference or asymmetric routing for a small subset of paths.
- High retry rate on queries to upstream resolver 172.20.8.5 with SERVFAIL and timeouts.
- A cluster of flows from Skyline IP block observed being NATed to the same ephemeral ports until conntrack entries aged out, which aligns with the port exhaustion theory.

I also checked our route re-apply audit: automated policy job #policy-982 ran at 11:31:12 UTC and touched routes for skyline-prod-peering. We're isolating whether the policy re-apply coincided with an infrastructure restart that produced transient NAT state.

Attachments: dns_trace_skyline_1130.pcap

--Jordan
Infrastructure Reliability Engineer
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Executive Leadership <leadership@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, ops@skyline-retail.com
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 17:02:00 +0000
Subject: Executive note — Skyline major customer impact and proposed remediation + credit authorization

Team,

Summary: Skyline Retail experienced a customer-impacting throughput and error event in us-west-1 beginning ~11:30 UTC. Root cause appears to be a convergence of (1) automated peering/route policy re-application, (2) transient upstream resolver failures, and (3) conntrack/NAT session exhaustion on a subset of egress gateways. The combination produced elevated latency and 5xxs for ~45 minutes.

Business impact: Skyline is a mid-market strategic account with active expansion discussions. They have requested an exec-level apology and asked about credits for the incident window. They also want confirmation we will not re-apply automated route policy changes during peak hours without a canary.

Proposed remediation and asks:
- Short term (in flight): complete gateway failover, increase conntrack thresholds, and pin Skyline's peering route to a static policy for 24 hours. (Marissa team executing.)
- Mid term: add a safety interlock to block automated route policy re-applies if NAT session utilization > 70% for any tenant. (Engineering/Platform work item.)
- Long term: introduce resolver fallback (multi-resolver and local caching) per VPC to reduce impact from upstream DNS blips. (Platform roadmap).

Credit authorization request: recommend offering Skyline a one-month service credit on their committed Dedicated plan and waive overage charges for the incident window. Approve? Please reply with any objections by EOD.

I will join an exec call with Skyline if they request. Ben, own the customer communication and timeline — coordinate with Marissa for the technical postmortem.

—Vivek
CTO, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 08:14:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Executive note — Skyline major customer impact and proposed remediation + credit authorization

Ack on the plan.
We completed gateway failover at 17:10 UTC and saw queues normalize within ~6 minutes. Conntrack thresholds were increased and the automation was paused. Jordan will follow up with a short tech write-up for the postmortem.

I'll create the engineering ticket for the automation interlock (JIRA-INC-4821) and assign to platform next sprint.

Marissa
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@skyline-retail.com>, ops@skyline-retail.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 10:22:00 +0000
Subject: Skyline — apology, mitigation summary, and next steps

Sarah / Skyline ops,

Thank you for your patience while our teams triaged this morning's incident. Apologies again for the disruption — we know this impacted your checkout flow.

What we did:
- Failed over traffic from the affected egress gateways and increased conntrack thresholds to avoid immediate port exhaustion.
- Paused the automated route policy job and pinned your peering route to a static policy for 24 hours while we stabilize.
- Collected PCAPs and resolver traces; shared a sanitized copy to your ops mailbox and our incident drive.

Next steps:
- We will deliver a short postmortem by EOD Wednesday with root cause analysis and clear mitigations.
- We propose a one-month credit on your Dedicated commitment for the incident window; we'll formalize and send the credit confirmation once leadership signs off.
- Platform will prioritize a resolver fallback + caching design to minimize blast radius from upstream DNS flaps.

Attachments: skyline_alert_screenshot.png

If you'd like an executive call, Vivek is available to join.

—Ben
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
